citation.title: Cephalometric norms in Japanese adults
citation.journal: Journal of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-08 (norms:compare a vs b exit 1, 21 differences). Every mean and SD agreed and was re-read from the page images of Table 4 (p. 133, PDF p. 5) and Tables 2-3 (p. 132, PDF p. 4): agree. Decisions: (1) range, 20 entries (a entered Table 4's Min-Max columns as range, b did not) → not entered: they are the sample's observed extremes, not a norm range (as for AlBarakati 2012); caveat. (2) #88 soft-tissue convexity a 'close', b 'same' → close: the paper prints the departure from straight (10.09) and the stored 169.91 is our conversion (merge notes). Merge-notes rulings applied: women's ANS-Gn 63.86 from Table 4 (Table 2 prints 63.20), noted on the row; HP is about SN − 7°, so the FH-referenced ids (#8, #9, #23, #61) are close; mandibular plane not stated → #23, #57 on Go-Me, close; Wits occlusal plane not stated → close. Selection class-I: Class I occlusion, minor or no crowding, good facial symmetry (p. 129); the sample was not chosen for its profile. Scale not-stated: no magnification statement. Table 4's by-sex hard-tissue rows used (Tables 1-2 repeat them, except the women's ANS-Gn and UI-NF height); Table 3 soft tissue is pooled (p. 130). Burstone's white columns not entered. Ruling P49 (8 Oct): #88 close -> same (the exact 180 − x conversion on the catalogue's own points is not a definition difference).

caveats: Sample: 217 Japanese adults (98 men, 119 women), 20-28 y, with Japanese grandparents; Class I occlusion with minor or no crowding, good facial symmetry, no orthodontic treatment or surgery; all Okayama University students (p. 129).
Radiographs in natural head position, teeth in maximum intercuspation, lips in repose (Shimavision 1100); hand traced and digitised in Quick Ceph (pp. 129-130). Film magnification not stated.
Hard-tissue measurements follow Burstone's COGS: many are referenced to HP, a horizontal plane through N at 7° to SN (Fig 1, p. 130), not to FH, so every HP-based entry is close.
Table 4 also prints each sex's range, minimum and maximum: the sample's observed extremes, not a norm range; not entered.

Women's lower anterior face height ANS-Gn (HP): Table 2 prints 63.20, Table 4 63.86 (SD 4.98 in both); Table 4 is used. Table 2 and Table 4 also differ for the women's UI-NF dental height (28.50 vs 28.57), not a catalogue measurement.
Soft-tissue values (Table 3) are for both sexes together; the paper says they were not split by sex (p. 130). Table 3 prints no n; 217 is the whole sample.
Soft-tissue convexity G-Sn-Pg′ is printed as the departure from a straight profile (10.09°); stored as the full angle 169.91° (180 − 10.09) to match the catalogue - our conversion.

Not in the catalogue: Ar-PTM and PtM-N (HP) cranial base, N-B (HP), N-ANS and PNS-N (HP) face heights, UI-NF, LI-MP, UM-NF, LM-MP dental heights, PNS-ANS (pHP), Ar-Go and Go-Pog lengths, B-Pg chin depth (Table 4); G-Sn and G-Pg′ (HP), G-Sn/Sn-Me′, Sn-Gn′-C, Sn-Gn′/C-Gn′, lip protrusion to Sn-Pg′, mentolabial sulcus to Li-Pg′, Sn-Stms/Stmi-Me′, Stms-UI, Stms-Stmi (Table 3).
